title: GitHub Integration Product Segment Map v1

segments.name: Solo Developer
segments.description: Individual developer working on personal, freelance, or indie projects. Uses GitHub for version control, issue tracking, CI, and occasionally static hosting.
pain_points: Browser-tab fragmentation: issues in one tab, PRs in another, Actions in a third, security alerts in a fourth — no unified view of repo health
GitHub CLI covers basic operations but has no dashboard, triage, or alert summarization
Context-switching between code editor and GitHub UI breaks flow and reduces productivity
No local-first evidence when things go wrong — debugging failed Actions or rejected PRs requires hunting through GitHub web UI
Free-tier limitations: GitHub Advanced Security not available, leaving code scanning and secret scanning gaps for solo developers who cannot afford GHAS
rig_relay_opportunity: Single cockpit unifying issues, PRs, Actions, security alerts, and repo health in one local desktop surface
Local-first evidence: every GitHub operation produces a content-light receipt stored locally, auditable without GitHub web UI
Governed mutations: dry-run-first, human-in-the-loop approval for any write operation — no surprise pushes
Agent-assisted issue triage: AI help with labeling, prioritization, and context collection without ever touching the repo without permission
Offline-capable: evidence and projections available even when GitHub is unreachable
required_ux_primitives: Compact repo health chip: single visual element showing open issues, open PRs, failed Actions, unread security alerts
Issue-to-mission one-click: convert a GitHub issue into a governed Rig Relay mission with context packet pre-populated
PR status inline: show PR CI status, review state, and mergeability without leaving cockpit
Action failure notification: proactive alert when a workflow run fails, linked to relevant logs
Security alert digest: daily/weekly summary of new code scanning, secret scanning, and Dependabot alerts
required_github_permissions: Read: metadata, issues, pull requests, code scanning alerts, repository contents (public repos unauthenticated; private repos via token/OAuth)
Write: gated behind explicit approval — issues (create/update), pull requests (create/review), repository contents (push, if owned)
No write permission by default; every mutation requires human confirmation in cockpit
required_governance_boundaries: Dry-run-first: every planned GitHub mutation produces a preview before execution; human must approve each step
Human-in-the-loop: no automated pushes, PR merges, or issue modifications without explicit cockpit confirmation
Content-light receipts: every API call produces a receipt with SHA256 hashes of content; raw content never stored in telemetry
No-surprise attribution: all agent-generated content explicitly labeled as such; co-authored-by headers transparent

Local operational evidence remains available; product telemetry is first-party and opt-out by default; remote contribution can be disabled; product telemetry opt-out degrades adaptive assistance but preserves governance evidence
telemetry_opportunity: Feature adoption patterns: which GitHub surfaces does the solo developer use most in cockpit vs. browser?
Frustration-signal detection: repeated browser tab opens for GitHub operations that could be in-cockpit
Workflow completion rates: how often do issue-to-mission and PR pipelines complete successfully?
Time savings measurement: reduction in context-switching by comparing cockpit usage vs. browser tab count
C1 note: 'no telemetry shared externally' term not present independently in segment map; remote telemetry contribution is separately controlled and enterprise-configurable
segments.enterprise_procurement_implications: Free for solo use, local-only. No enterprise procurement needed. Open-source (AGPL-3.0). No vendor lock-in: evidence artifacts are portable JSON/JSONL. GitHub account required for private repos; public repos work without auth.
what_would_make_them_switch: Unified cockpit eliminates 4-5 browser tabs for routine GitHub operations
Governed agent assistance that never surprises: dry-run previews before any write
Local-first evidence archive that makes GitHub web UI feel slow and fragmented by comparison
Offline access to repo state, issues, and PRs when GitHub is down or network is slow
Free and open-source, unlike GitHub Advanced Security or paid CI dashboards

segments.name: Open-Source Maintainer
segments.description: Maintainer of one or more open-source projects with community contributors. Manages issues, PRs, releases, security, and community health.
pain_points: Triage overload: popular repos receive dozens of issues and PRs daily; manual triage doesn't scale
Spam PRs: low-quality or malicious PRs waste maintainer time and pollute the review queue
Security alert fatigue: Dependabot and code scanning produce many alerts; prioritization is manual and error-prone
Contributor onboarding friction: CLA checking, first-contribution guidance, and style-guide enforcement are fragmented across tools
No transparent provenance: when using AI assistance, unclear what was human-written vs. agent-generated, risking community trust erosion
rig_relay_opportunity: Automated triage queue: AI-assisted labeling, priority scoring, and spam detection for issues and PRs
Code scanning alert prioritization: rank alerts by exploitability, reachability, and blast radius — not just severity
Dependabot batch update planning: group related dependency updates, test them together, and produce a single governed PR
Contributor CLA/permission audit: verify CLA signature, check contribution history, and flag first-time contributors for extra guidance
Transparent agent provenance: every agent-generated line is attributed; no hidden co-authorship; community trust preserved
required_ux_primitives: Security queue with severity scoring: ranked list of code scanning, secret scanning, and Dependabot alerts with Rich context packets
PR review packet with risk summary: per-PR summary of change size, test status, CLA status, code scanning results, and review complexity score
Stale issue detection: auto-flag issues with no activity beyond threshold, propose closing or re-triage
Contributor dashboard: per-contributor stats, CLA status, first-PR flag, and contribution quality trends
Release checklist panel: verify all gates (tests pass, changelog updated, version bumped, security advisories reviewed) before tagging
required_github_permissions: Read: public repos unrestricted; all issue/PR/security alert metadata; repository contents for owned repos
Write: gated for owned repos only — issue management (label/close/assign), PR management (request changes/approve), branch operations (create/delete)
No write access to forked contributor repos; all mutations require explicit maintainer approval
required_governance_boundaries: Explicit attribution on all generated content: every agent-authored comment, review, or PR description carries visible attribution
No marketing in PRs/comments: agent-generated content must not include promotional language, product pitches, or irrelevant links
Community-trust preservation: agent behavior must match the project's code of conduct; never dismissive, never spammy
Dry-run for all automated responses: proposed issue responses and PR reviews shown as previews before posting
No autonomous commenting: agent may draft responses but never posts them without maintainer approval
Community trust and provenance remain independent of telemetry settings; governance evidence continuity is mandatory regardless of telemetry opt-out status
telemetry_opportunity: Community health metrics: response time to new issues, PR review turnaround, contributor retention rate
Alert resolution velocity: time from code scanning alert publication to remediation PR merge
Triage efficiency: percentage of issues/PRs correctly auto-labeled, auto-assigned, or auto-prioritized
Spam detection accuracy: false positive rate for PR spam detection, reviewed manually
segments.enterprise_procurement_implications: Free for open-source use. No GitHub Advanced Security license required for Rig Relay's own scanning and prioritization (consumes existing public alert data). GitHub App install for private repos uses free-tier permissions. No vendor lock-in: all triage decisions, alert states, and agent receipts are portable JSONL artifacts.
what_would_make_them_switch: AI-assisted triage that actually reduces inbox zero time, not adds noise
Governed agent PRs that never pollute: every automated change is previewed, attributed, and reversible
Transparent provenance for every agent-assisted action — community trust is non-negotiable
Batch security alert remediation planning that groups related fixes into single, testable PRs
Free for open source; no per-seat or per-repo pricing

segments.name: Small Team (2-15)
segments.description: Co-located or distributed small engineering team building a product together. Uses GitHub for collaboration, CI/CD, and project management.
pain_points: Inconsistent code review quality: different team members apply different review standards; no shared checklist or risk-scoring framework
Missed security alerts: alerts buried in GitHub notifications; no team-level visibility into who owns which alert
Deployment coordination: no shared view of what's in pre-production vs. production across branches and environments
Knowledge silos: one person knows the CI config, another knows the deployment pipeline; no shared operating picture
Fragmented notifications: GitHub emails, Slack mentions, in-app notifications — no unified, prioritized feed
rig_relay_opportunity: Team-shared cockpit projections: WebSocket-projected repo state visible to all team members in real time
PR review packet standardization: every PR gets the same structured risk summary, test results, and review checklist
Security posture dashboard: team-level view of open alerts, assigned owners, and resolution timelines
Release readiness panel: shared checklist showing all gates (tests, security, changelog, approvals) for every pending release
Unified notification feed: GitHub events normalized into a single, prioritized, governable stream with team assignment
required_ux_primitives: Team activity feed: chronological, filterable stream of GitHub events (commits, PRs, issues, alerts, deployments) with owner tags
Review queue: prioritized list of PRs needing review, sorted by urgency (security fixes first), with risk summaries
Branch protection health: visual indicator of which branches have protection rules enabled and whether CI passes on latest commit
Deployment status: per-environment status (dev, staging, production) showing which commit is deployed and whether checks passed
Security ownership matrix: per-alert-type assignment showing who owns code scanning, secret scanning, and Dependabot triage
required_github_permissions: Read: repository metadata, issues, pull requests, code scanning alerts, Actions workflow runs, branch protection rules (team-scoped GitHub App install)
Write: gated — PR review (approve/request changes/comment), issue assignment/labeling, branch creation (protected branches need admin approval)
Admin: gated for designated team leads — branch protection changes, repository settings modifications
required_governance_boundaries: Team-level approval chains: mutations requiring admin access need designated approver sign-off
Audit trail for all agent actions: every agent-assisted review, comment, or label change produces a receipt visible to the whole team
No silent mutations: any agent-originated change must be visible in the team feed with clear attribution
Permission escalation prevention: no agent or team member can escalate their own permissions without admin approval
Review quality standards: agent-assisted reviews must meet team-defined checklist criteria; below-threshold reviews flagged
Operational dashboards use local/enterprise evidence; product telemetry opt-out does not remove team audit trail or governance evidence
telemetry_opportunity: Team velocity: issue-to-merge cycle time, PR review turnaround, deployment frequency
Review cycle time: time from PR open to first review, from first review to merge, segmented by reviewer
Security debt trend: open alerts over time, resolution velocity, mean time to remediate by severity
Knowledge-silo detection: which repos/paths have only one active contributor, flagging bus-factor risk
segments.enterprise_procurement_implications: Small-team tier: free or low-cost per-seat. GitHub App install scoped to team repos. Portable JSONL evidence enables compliance readiness without enterprise procurement overhead. No vendor lock-in: all projections, review packets, and audit trails are exportable.
what_would_make_them_switch: Replaces fragmented GitHub notifications with a structured, prioritized, governed team feed
Standardized PR review packets enforce consistent quality without adding process overhead
Team-wide security posture visibility eliminates 'I thought you were handling that' alert gaps
Shared cockpit projections give every team member the same operating picture, dissolving knowledge silos
Agent-assisted reviews that save time without compromising quality or attribution

segments.name: Startup Engineering Org (15-100)
segments.description: Growing startup with multiple engineering teams, several repos, and increasing compliance and operational maturity requirements.
pain_points: Velocity vs. security tradeoffs: pressure to ship fast leads to skipped reviews, bypassed branch protection, and ignored security alerts
Compliance readiness: investors, enterprise customers, or auditors ask for security posture evidence that doesn't exist in organized form
Multi-repo coordination: changes span multiple repos; no unified view of cross-repo PRs, releases, or deployments
On-call noise: Actions failures, deployment rollbacks, and incident alerts are fragmented across tools; no single pane for investigation
Tool sprawl: separate tools for code review, CI visibility, security scanning, project management, and incident response
rig_relay_opportunity: Multi-repo portfolio view: unified dashboard showing health, security posture, and release status across all org repos
Compliance posture dashboard: SOC2/ISO27001 evidence generation from content-light GitHub data — alerts, reviews, deployments, access changes
Incident timeline reconstruction: correlated timeline of commits, PRs, deployments, and alerts for any incident investigation period
Enterprise procurement readiness: start building the evidence pack now so enterprise sales conversations don't stall on security reviews
Tool consolidation: replace fragmented CI dashboards, security scanners, and project trackers with a single governed cockpit
required_ux_primitives: Org-level security posture: aggregated alert counts, remediation velocity, and compliance score across all repos
Release readiness across repos: per-repo and cross-repo release checklist showing gate status for all pending releases
Cost/rate-limit dashboard: GitHub API rate-limit consumption, Actions minutes used, and projected costs
Cross-repo PR tracker: view all open PRs across repos with dependency ordering (PR B depends on PR A being merged first)
Incident reconstruction timeline: select a time window, see all GitHub events (commits, merges, deployments, alerts) in chronological order
required_github_permissions: Read: org-scoped GitHub App with metadata, issues, pull requests, code scanning alerts, Actions, branch protection, and audit log events
Write: gated — PR review, issue management, branch operations (protected branches need separate approval)
Admin: org-level changes gated behind CTO/engineering-lead approval; no agent access to org admin APIs
Least-privilege: separate GitHub App installations for read-only projection vs. governed mutation lanes
required_governance_boundaries: SOC2/ISO27001 evidence generation: every governed action produces structured evidence mapped to compliance control frameworks
Change approval workflows: mutations that affect protected branches, environments, or org settings require multi-party approval
Audit trail completeness: every GitHub API call through Rig Relay produces a timestamped, SHA256-hashed receipt
Separation of duties: projection (read-only) and mutation (write) paths use separate GitHub App tokens with different permission scopes
Immutable evidence: JSONL artifacts are append-only; no evidence can be modified or deleted after creation
Compliance evidence generation is not disabled by product telemetry opt-out; enterprise audit continuity is mandatory
telemetry_opportunity: Compliance posture trends: security debt over time, review coverage percentage, branch protection compliance rate
Security debt velocity: new alerts per week vs. alerts resolved per week; trend direction indicates security maturity
Cross-repo dependency health: how often cross-repo PR chains break; which repos are most coupled
Tool consolidation savings: reduction in paid tools replaced by Rig Relay cockpit — direct cost savings metric
segments.enterprise_procurement_implications: Startup tier: per-seat pricing with compliance evidence pack included. GitHub App installs across org repos. Portable evidence artifacts support enterprise sales security reviews. Migration path to enterprise tier when org crosses 100 engineers. No vendor lock-in: all compliance evidence is exportable JSONL/CSV.
what_would_make_them_switch: Demonstrates enterprise-grade security posture without enterprise overhead — passes customer security reviews
Unified multi-repo cockpit replaces 3-5 separate tools, reducing both cost and cognitive load
Compliance evidence generation is automatic, not a manual quarterly scramble
Incident investigation that takes minutes instead of hours by correlating all GitHub events in one timeline
Governed agent behavior that accelerates development without sacrificing security or review quality

segments.name: Security-Conscious Enterprise
segments.description: Enterprise with dedicated security team, compliance requirements (SOC2, ISO27001, FedRAMP), and zero-trust architecture. Uses GitHub Advanced Security.
pain_points: GitHub Advanced Security cost: per-committer pricing scales poorly for large organizations; many repos go unprotected due to budget
Alert fatigue at scale: thousands of code scanning, secret scanning, and Dependabot alerts with no effective triage or prioritization
Compliance audit overhead: auditors request evidence of review processes, access controls, and change management — GitHub audit log is verbose and hard to query
Permission sprawl: GitHub App permissions are coarse-grained; no visibility into which integrations have what access across repos
Provenance gaps: when using AI coding assistants, no chain of custody from prompt to commit to PR to merge — compliance teams cannot attest to code origin
rig_relay_opportunity: Governed security pipeline: intake, triage, prioritization, remediation planning, and governed PR creation — all producing content-light evidence
Permission posture reporting: catalog every GitHub App installation across orgs, their permission scopes, last-used timestamps, and risk scores
Audit-log ingestion and enrichment: consume GitHub audit log events, normalize them, and produce queryable, timeline-correlated evidence
Least-privilege enforcement: Rig Relay's own GitHub App uses read-only defaults; every write operation requires explicit approval and produces a receipt
Provenance chain: from agent prompt to SHA256-hashed commit to governed PR to merge — every step produces immutable evidence suitable for compliance attestation
required_ux_primitives: Security posture panel: org-wide dashboard of open alerts by type, severity, repo, and age; remediation velocity trends; SLA compliance
Permission matrix viewer: interactive grid showing every GitHub App, its permissions, which repos it accesses, last activity, and risk classification
Audit event timeline: queryable, filterable timeline of all GitHub audit log events, enriched with Rig Relay governance receipts
Code scanning/secret scanning/Dependabot triage queue: unified alert queue with Rich context packets, severity scoring, and assignment
Branch protection compliance report: per-repo and org-wide view of branch protection rule status, violations, and drift detection
required_github_permissions: Read: read-only GitHub App default for metadata, code scanning alerts, secret scanning alerts, Dependabot alerts, audit log, branch protection rules, repository content (for analysis)
Write: gated behind explicit approval with attestation signing — PR creation, issue management, branch operations
Admin: no admin access by default; admin operations require separate approval workflow with multi-party sign-off
Token scoping: separate token profiles for read-only analysis, governed mutation, and admin operations
required_governance_boundaries: HMAC-SHA256 attestation signing: every governed mutation is cryptographically signed; attestations are verifiable independently of Rig Relay
Append-only JSONL evidence: all security pipeline artifacts, permission changes, and agent actions are recorded in immutable JSONL streams
Replayable audit trail: entire security pipeline history can be replayed from JSONL evidence for auditor review

Product telemetry is first-party and opt-out by default; remote contribution is separately controlled and enterprise-configurable; enterprise audit/evidence continuity is mandatory; no raw repo content, tokens, secrets, prompts, completions, diffs, Actions logs, or secret fragments in any data stream
Explicit human review for all mutations: no agent can create a PR, modify a branch, or change permissions without human approval in cockpit
Product telemetry disabled must not disable enterprise GitHub audit/evidence continuity
telemetry_opportunity: Security posture trends: alert volume over time, MTTR by severity, SLA compliance percentage
Permission hygiene: stale App installations, over-privileged tokens, unused permissions detected
Pipeline efficiency: intake-to-remediation cycle time, false positive rate for auto-prioritization
Compliance readiness score: percentage of required evidence artifacts available and valid
segments.enterprise_procurement_implications: Enterprise tier: per-seat pricing with volume discounts. Security questionnaire evidence pack included (architecture diagram, data flow, encryption at rest/transit, access controls, audit trail, incident response). Data residency: all evidence artifacts are local-first; no data leaves the enterprise boundary unless explicitly configured. SOC2/ISO27001 mapping available. Penetration test evidence available. Procurement review package includes RBAC model, tenant isolation architecture, attestation signing specification, and redaction policy.
what_would_make_them_switch: Content-light, auditable, replayable evidence that GitHub native audit log cannot match — auditors can verify independently
Governed agent behavior with no surprise mutation — every agent action is previewed, approved, and receipted
Permission posture visibility across all GitHub Apps — finally answering 'who has access to what?'
Security alert prioritization that cuts through fatigue by ranking by exploitability, not just severity
No raw content leakage in telemetry — enterprise can prove to auditors that Rig Relay never exposed source code

segments.name: Massive Technology Corporation (1000+)
segments.description: Large enterprise with GitHub Enterprise Cloud or Server, multiple organizations, thousands of repositories, dedicated platform engineering and security teams.
pain_points: GitHub Enterprise Cloud/Server fragmentation: some teams on Cloud, others on Server; no unified governance or visibility across instances
Multi-org governance: each organization has its own GitHub App installs, permission models, and security policies — no central enforcement point
Thousands of repos: impossible to manually audit branch protection, security alert status, or permission hygiene across all repos
Compliance at scale: auditors demand consistent evidence across all orgs and repos; manual collection is infeasible
Procurement complexity: enterprise buyers need security architecture diagrams, pen-test results, SOC2 reports, data-flow maps, and integration compatibility matrices before purchase
rig_relay_opportunity: Multi-org portfolio analytics: fleet-wide dashboard aggregating security posture, compliance status, and operational health across all orgs and instances
Enterprise policy engine: define security and governance policies centrally; enforce them across all orgs; detect and report drift
Fleet orchestration: governed agent lanes that operate across orgs with scoped permissions per org, producing unified evidence
Centralized evidence store: all GitHub-derived evidence (alerts, audit logs, permission postures, agent receipts) stored in a single queryable substrate
Enterprise procurement pack: comprehensive security and architecture documentation generated from the same content-light evidence pipeline
required_ux_primitives: Enterprise admin panel: central console for managing GitHub App installs, permission profiles, policy definitions, and compliance reports across all orgs
Org-level compliance dashboard: per-org and fleet-wide compliance scores, drift detection, and remediation recommendations
Fleet-wide security posture: aggregated alert counts, remediation velocity, and SLA compliance across all orgs
Rate-limit budget across orgs: monitor and allocate GitHub API rate-limit consumption across orgs to prevent noisy-neighbor issues
Repository allowlist/denylist management: centrally control which repos Rig Relay can access across all orgs
required_github_permissions: Read: enterprise-scoped GitHub App with metadata, audit log, code/secret/Dependabot alerts, branch protection, and repository contents across all authorized orgs
Write: per-org, per-repo gating with separate approval workflows; no cross-org write capability
Admin: enterprise-level admin operations require designated platform-engineering-team approval
Allowlist/denylist: centrally managed repository access control; repos outside allowlist are invisible to Rig Relay
required_governance_boundaries: SSO/SAML/SCIM-adjacent planning: Rig Relay must integrate with enterprise identity providers for authentication and authorization
Enterprise audit-log ingestion: consume and normalize GitHub Enterprise audit log events across all orgs
Data residency controls: evidence artifacts stored in enterprise-controlled infrastructure; no data leaves approved regions
Cross-org isolation: agent operations in one org must never leak data or permissions into another org
Policy-as-code: security and governance policies defined as version-controlled configuration, not UI checkboxes
Enterprise policy may disable remote telemetry contribution; enterprise audit/evidence remains mandatory regardless
telemetry_opportunity: Fleet-wide health: aggregated metrics across orgs — alert resolution velocity, compliance drift rate, permission hygiene score
Platform adoption: which orgs and teams are using Rig Relay; which GitHub surfaces are most used
Policy enforcement rate: percentage of repos compliant with enterprise policies; drift detection frequency
Rate-limit efficiency: API call volume by org, by operation type; optimization recommendations
segments.enterprise_procurement_implications: Enterprise volume licensing: per-seat pricing with fleet-wide discounts. Dedicated procurement evidence pack: security architecture, pen-test results, SOC2/ISO27001 mapping, data-flow diagrams, RBAC model, tenant isolation documentation, attestation signing specification. Support for GitHub Enterprise Cloud and Server. Data residency: all evidence artifacts local-first with enterprise-controlled storage. SSO/SAML/SCIM integration support. Dedicated onboarding and migration support. Custom policy engine configuration.
what_would_make_them_switch: Unified governance across GitHub Enterprise Cloud and Server — no other tool provides single-pane visibility across instances
Portable evidence artifacts that survive tool changes — JSONL evidence is forever, regardless of which vendor provides the cockpit
Fleet-wide agent orchestration with per-org permission boundaries — governed AI at enterprise scale
Centralized compliance dashboard eliminates months of manual evidence collection for annual audits
Procurement evidence pack that answers security team questions before they're asked — accelerates enterprise buying cycles

segments.name: Agency/Consultant Managing Many Repos
segments.description: Development agency, consultancy, or freelance collective managing GitHub repos for multiple clients simultaneously.
pain_points: Context-switching across client repos: different orgs, different permission models, different security postures — no unified operating picture
Inconsistent security posture: each client has different security requirements; agency cannot enforce consistent standards across all managed repos
Billing/procurement complexity: agency needs to show client-specific value, not aggregate metrics; evidence of work done per client is manual
Accidental cross-client contamination: risk of pushing to wrong client's repo, using wrong credentials, or leaking client A's code to client B's environment
Permission management overhead: adding/removing team members across multiple GitHub orgs is error-prone and time-consuming
rig_relay_opportunity: Multi-client portfolio view: one cockpit with per-client tabs, each showing that client's repos, security posture, and agent activity
Per-client permission boundaries: separate GitHub App installs per client with isolated authentication; impossible to cross-contaminate
Automated security scanning across all managed repos: uniform security posture assessment regardless of client's own GitHub configuration
Per-client evidence packs: generate client-specific reports showing work done, security improvements, and agent activity — no raw data leakage between clients
Team management: assign agency team members to specific client lanes with scoped permissions
required_ux_primitives: Client-switching cockpit: quick-switch between client contexts; each context shows only that client's repos, alerts, and activity
Per-client security dashboard: security posture, open alerts, and remediation progress scoped to each client
Billing/procurement evidence pack: per-client summary of governed operations, security improvements, and agent activity suitable for client reporting
Cross-client isolation indicator: always-visible indicator confirming which client context is active; prevent accidental cross-client operations
Team assignment matrix: per-client, per-repo assignment of agency team members with role-based access
required_github_permissions: Read: per-client GitHub App installs with isolated authentication; each client's data is completely separated
Write: per-client gating — PR creation, issue management, and branch operations scoped to specific client repos only
No shared credentials across clients: each client connection uses a distinct GitHub App installation with its own token lifecycle
required_governance_boundaries: Tenant-scoped evidence: all JSONL artifacts, audit trails, and agent receipts are tagged with client identifier; cross-client access is impossible at the data layer
Cross-client data isolation: agency operators cannot view client A's data while in client B's context; enforced at both UI and data layers
Per-client dry-run and approval: mutations for each client require approval within that client's context
No client-data aggregation: analytics and telemetry are per-client; no aggregate view that could leak competitive information between clients
Clear client attribution: all agent-generated content (PRs, issues, comments) carries client-appropriate attribution, not agency branding
telemetry_opportunity: Per-client velocity: issue resolution time, PR merge rate, security alert response time — all per-client, never cross-client
Agency efficiency: average time per client context-switch, tool adoption across clients
Security improvement tracking: per-client security posture trend over time, demonstrating agency value
Client retention signals: which features drive continued engagement; which friction points precede client churn
segments.enterprise_procurement_implications: Agency tier: per-client-seat pricing. Multi-client GitHub App management built in. Per-client evidence exports for client billing and reporting. No vendor lock-in: each client's evidence artifacts are portable and can be handed to the client if the agency relationship ends. Cross-client isolation is architecturally enforced, not just policy-enforced — auditable by third parties.
what_would_make_them_switch: One cockpit for N clients — eliminates the mental overhead of managing multiple GitHub orgs across multiple browser windows
Per-client governed agent lanes that never leak data or permissions between clients
Client-specific evidence packs that demonstrate value and justify retainers — automated, not manual
Architecturally enforced cross-client isolation that passes client security reviews
Uniform security posture assessment across all clients regardless of their own GitHub configuration

segments.name: AI-Agent-Heavy Engineering Team
segments.description: Engineering team that heavily uses AI coding assistants (Copilot, Cursor, Claude, etc.) and needs governance, audit, and control over agent GitHub activity.
pain_points: Agent-produced PR pollution: AI tools create PRs with unclear provenance, unverified correctness, and no review accountability
Unclear authorship: who wrote this code — the human, the agent, or a mix? Compliance, legal, and open-source licensing implications are unclear
Surprise mutations: agents pushing commits, creating branches, or opening PRs without explicit human intent or approval
Permission overreach: AI tools request broad GitHub permissions (read/write all repos) with no least-privilege scoping
Provenance gaps: when something goes wrong, there's no chain of custody from prompt to commit to merge; impossible to audit agent behavior
rig_relay_opportunity: Governed agent lanes: every AI agent operates within explicitly permissioned boundaries; no agent can access GitHub beyond its assigned scope
Agent-produced evidence timeline: every agent action (prompt received, tool called, API request sent, response received) produces an immutable receipt
Agent attribution and provenance: every commit, PR, and comment carries explicit agent attribution; no hidden or ambiguous authorship
Agent behavior audit: queryable timeline of all agent GitHub activity across the team — what did each agent do, when, and with what permissions?
Permission scoping per agent: different agents get different GitHub App token profiles; code reviewers get read-only, code generators get gated write
required_ux_primitives: Agent activity feed: chronological stream of all agent GitHub actions (reads, writes, reviews, comments) with agent identity, permission used, and outcome
Agent permission matrix: grid showing each registered agent, its GitHub App permissions, which repos it can access, and when permissions were last verified
Agent-produced PR queue with risk summary: PRs created by agents shown with risk scoring, change size, test status, and approval required
Agent governance dashboard: team-level view of agent activity metrics, policy violations, and permission hygiene
Agent context viewer: for any agent-produced artifact, view the chain of prompts, tool calls, and receipts that produced it
required_github_permissions: Read: per-agent read-only token profiles for code exploration, review, and analysis agents
Write: per-agent gated write profiles for code generation agents — PR creation, branch operations, issue management
No agent gets write access by default; every write-enabled agent requires explicit team-lead approval
Per-repo scoping: agents are assigned to specific repos, not org-wide access
required_governance_boundaries: Every agent action produces a receipt: prompts, tool calls, API requests, and responses are recorded as immutable JSONL artifacts
Agent mutations blocked by default: no agent can create a PR, push a commit, or modify a branch without explicit human approval
Human review required for remote mutations: before any agent-created PR is submitted to GitHub, a human reviews and approves in cockpit
Attribution transparency: all agent-generated content (commits, PR descriptions, comments, reviews) carries visible agent attribution
Permission escalation impossible: agents cannot request, escalate, or modify their own GitHub permissions; only human admins can change agent permissions
Agent behavior telemetry used for optimization unless disabled; no raw repo content, prompts, completions, or secrets leave the local boundary; remote telemetry contribution is separately controlled
telemetry_opportunity: Agent productivity: PRs created, issues resolved, reviews completed per agent — with human-approval rate overlay
Agent safety metrics: percentage of agent actions blocked by governance, approval denial rate, permission hygiene score
Agent drift detection: changes in agent behavior patterns over time — is an agent getting more aggressive? requesting more permissions?
Team adoption: which agents are most used, which permission profiles are most common, what approval patterns emerge
segments.enterprise_procurement_implications: Included in enterprise tier. Per-agent seat pricing if distinct from human seats. Agent governance evidence pack included: agent activity audit, permission matrix, provenance chains, attestation signatures. Integration with enterprise SSO/RBAC for agent identity. Procurement evidence demonstrating agent governance superiority over raw GitHub Copilot or direct API access.
what_would_make_them_switch: Rig Relay is the only tool that governs agent GitHub access with content-light, auditable, replayable evidence
Agent permission scoping that gives teams confidence to use AI without fear of surprise mutations
Complete provenance chain for every agent action — satisfies legal, compliance, and open-source licensing requirements
Agent governance dashboard gives team leads visibility they currently lack over AI coding assistant behavior
Per-agent permission profiles eliminate the 'one token to rule them all' problem of direct GitHub App installations

segments.name: Non-Expert Business Owner (Static Site)
segments.description: Business owner, content creator, or non-technical stakeholder who needs to manage a GitHub Pages website without learning Git or GitHub.
pain_points: GitHub too technical: Git concepts (commit, push, branch, merge, PR) are intimidating and unnecessary for simple content updates
Pages deployment confusing: understanding Jekyll, GitHub Actions, or YAML frontmatter is a barrier to making simple text changes
Content updates require developer help: every typo fix or content change needs a developer's time, creating bottlenecks and cost
No visibility into what changed: after making a change, unclear whether it deployed, what the live site looks like now, or what changed
Fear of breaking things: accidental deletion, wrong formatting, or broken links are hard to detect and harder to fix without developer help
rig_relay_opportunity: Governed static site editing: simple content editor with preview, version history, and one-click deploy — no Git knowledge required
One-click deploy with preview: see exactly what the site will look like before publishing; deploy with a single button
Content-light evidence of changes: every edit produces a receipt showing what changed, when, and by whom — transparent without Git jargon
Safe editing: dry-run preview means nothing goes live without explicit confirmation; impossible to accidentally break the site
Developer handoff when needed: for complex changes beyond content editing, generate a governed mission for a developer agent
required_ux_primitives: Simple content editor: WYSIWYG or plain-text editor for static site content (markdown, HTML, text) with live preview
Preview panel: render the site as it will appear on GitHub Pages, with navigation, styling, and responsive layout preview
Deploy button: single-click deployment with progress indicator; no Git commands, no PR workflow, no YAML configuration
Change history: timeline of all content changes with before/after previews and receipts — like a simplified git log
Help-request button: when something is beyond content editing, generate a governed mission for a developer agent to handle
required_github_permissions: Read: repository contents limited to Pages source directory (configurable per repo)
Write: gated content updates to Pages source only — no access to code, configuration, workflows, or other repo content
No branch or PR operations exposed; deployment uses a governed pipeline that abstracts away Git mechanics
required_governance_boundaries: Limited scope: Rig Relay's GitHub access is restricted to the Pages content directory; no access to source code, CI, or repo settings
Dry-run deploy preview: every content change previews the full site before any write to GitHub
No Git exposure: the UI never shows branches, commits, merges, or PRs; all deployment is abstracted into 'publish' or 'revert'
Revert capability: one-click undo for recent content changes — internally a git revert, but presented as 'undo last change'
Shared access control: business owner can grant content-editor access to team members without granting full GitHub access
telemetry_opportunity: Content update frequency: how often business users make changes without developer help
Preview-to-publish rate: how often a previewed change is actually published vs. abandoned
Developer handoff rate: how often a help-request mission is generated for content beyond the editor's capability
Adoption and retention: do non-technical users continue using the cockpit after initial onboarding?
segments.enterprise_procurement_implications: Included in team/startup/enterprise tiers as a value-add for non-technical stakeholders. For agencies managing client sites, available as a client-facing content editor portal. No separate pricing tier — this segment benefits the developer segments by reducing their support burden.
what_would_make_them_switch: Makes GitHub Pages accessible to non-developers without exposing raw GitHub complexity
One-click deploy with preview eliminates the fear of breaking the live site
No more waiting for developer availability to fix a typo or update content
Change history gives visibility and accountability without requiring Git knowledge
Safe editing with dry-run preview means business owners can experiment without risk
